title: Enable or disable the firewall via terminal
summary: Use the `m` command-line tool to toggle the macOS firewall. Disabling the firewall can help troubleshoot network connectivity issues, but it should be re-enabled afterwards for security.

steps.explain: Run the command to disable the firewall. Replace disable with enable to turn it back on.

placeholders.name: ACTION
placeholders.description: Use disable to turn off the firewall, or enable to turn it on.

rollback.explain: Re-enable the firewall to restore network security.

placeholders.name: ACTION
placeholders.description: Use enable to turn the firewall back on.

warnings: Disabling the firewall exposes your Mac to potential network threats. Only do this temporarily for troubleshooting.
